source_facts.fact: az account show --subscription selects cached subscription metadata; this is local selection correspondence, not remote authorization/revocation refresh.

get-access-token obtains selected account via same explicitsubscription, constructs credential, then acquire_token(scopes). Tool may satisfy token acquisition through its ordinary cache/provider behavior; no new interactive login/switch/refresh logic should be injected by Ashlar.

Token-held HTTP submission invokes no CLI interpreter/packages. Rehashing CLI bytes cannot establish Fabric authorization; successful/denied Fabric responses remain authoritative only for that actual operation.

recommended_boundary.credential_execution: One explicitly selected bounded credential-acquisition phase owns exact CLI/runtime/configuration/source/profile. Full selected closure content/inventory/link correspondence at opening and independent closing surrounds actual account-before/token/account-after commands. Execute real selection checks, private token response and exactexpiry/type/header/resource/correspondence admission. No arbitrary caller executable+digest/admission callback. Retain selected owner until release.
recommended_boundary.token_held_http: Every HTTP operation renews owner lifetime and original immutable config/context/token identity, remaining expiry/deadline/cumulative limits, exact permitted method/route/body, TLS trust and actual endpoint response. It does not execute or load CLI code; do not pretend CLI rehash is currentremotepermission. No token refresh/retry/fallback/cache of prior API authorization. Existing publication/source/ACK/no-mixed gates remain independent and unchanged.
recommended_boundary.closing: Independently attempt current original local runtime/configuration/account correspondence through selected CLI owner at close; reject drift and withhold combined qualification. Closing does not roll back already submitted permitted requests. Full original runtime bytes checked before and after each credential-execution interval according to admitted custody profile; no stat-only proof.
recommended_boundary.account_use_requirement: Current governing contract explicitly requires account/runtime correspondence at use. This cannot be silently removed. Governed amendment must choose and justify either token-held use (immutable captured account/token scope with no CLI invocation), or continued actual per-use accountshow (then that is another credentialtool execution interval with its required runtime custody). Call this a change of auth lifetime semantics, not a performance exception.

trusted_platform_assumptions: Operator-admitted genuine supported Homebrew AzureCLI installation/profile is trusted as credentialtool; a caller manifest/SHA is not toolidentity authority. Exact support must be version/platform qualified from observed actual2.90/runtime3.14.8, not stalepyvenv3.14.7.

OS kernel/process loader, Darwin system frameworks/libraries, selectedhost user/isolation and package deployment provenance are named trustedplatform dependencies outside content-manifest proof; package/nativeclosure inside claimed subset must still be enumerated and checked.

Full opening/closing hashes do not prove absence of transient midinterval mutation/reversion. If reducing perexecution checks relies on deployment immutability, name actual enforcement (readonly stable deployment/snapshot/exclusive cooperating writer scope) and scope proof; existing shared Homebrew tree has not yet provided such evidence. Do not claim descriptor/mtime checks or an Ashlar-only lock exclude other writers.

Selected explicit CLI config owner/privateidentity and actualCLI commands handle authstate; do not read credentialcache files to fabricate an immutable fullconfig snapshot. Nonsecret startup settings/extensions/env/TLS must be separately closed and qualified.
HTTP Python/TLS runtime has its own admitted selected trust profile; CLI closure hashes do not establish HTTP runtime/TLS custody.
